Local pnpm test on Windows exits 0 with a nonzero Test Files count line; every previously-red test is either fixed in its owning package or quarantined with a filed follow-up task id in the quarantine note.

"Build the Windows Job native binaries" — `cargo build --locked --release --manifest-path packages/runner/src/platform/windows/native/Cargo.toml --target-dir dist/windows-job-native -p moe-windows-job-broker`. This is ENVIRONMENT PARITY, not an extra gate leg: `dist/` is git-ignored (.gitignore:4), so a runner has no broker/spawner binaries while a dev box does — which is the only reason `pnpm test` passes locally. windows-boundary.test.ts asserts `resolveBrokerBinary()` resolves to a string, and its module states "a missing binary must FAIL rather than degrade", so guarding those suites with a skipIf would contradict the owning task's design AND make the lane read green while testing less. 2. The Test leg asserts its COUNT LINE instead of trusting exit 0 (`Select-String -Pattern '^\s*Test Files\s+[1-9][0-9]* passed'`), and republishes a refusal as a `::error::` annotation, matching what the host-evidence job does for the same reason. It also pins `$ErrorActionPreference = 'Continue'` and `$PSNativeCommandUseErrorActionPreference = $false` first: a pwsh step defaults to Stop, under which a native command's redirected stderr — git's harmless "LF will be replaced by CRLF" warning appears in this very run — can abort the step before the run is graded. `$LASTEXITCODE` after the pipeline is pnpm's, because a cmdlet like Tee-Object does not touch it; that is the pwsh equivalent of the PIPESTATUS read the bash jobs perform.

Scope decision recorded in the job's header comment as instructed: test:integration stays OUT of the required lane for v0.1 (it needs the packaging typecheck, the artifact task's own gates exercise it, and the MSYS tar hazard behind it is Git-Bash-local rather than something a pwsh runner reproduces); revisit at v0.2. THE TWO CI-ONLY DEFECT CLASSES, both root-caused:
A. 8.3 SHORT PATHS (~55 of the original 61). windows-latest hands a job `C:\Users\RUNNER~1\AppData\Local\Temp` because the account name exceeds eight characters, and Node then disagrees with ITSELF: `fs.realpathSync` (the JS implementation) leaves RUNNER~1 alone while `fs.promises.realpath` (libuv) expands it to runneradmin. A fixture root taken with one and a production realpath taken with the other differ by exactly that segment, so containment checks fire — 36x "escapes the fixture's native root", plus PHASE0_NODE_SOURCE_PATH_ESCAPE and CLAUDE_RUNTIME_PATH_ESCAPE. Fixed by pinning the JOB's TEMP/TMP to RUNNER_TEMP (D:\a\_temp, no 8.3 alias) — the environment a normal Windows box already has, which is why the same suite is green locally. Governor APPROVED as-shipped: "environment normalization, not gate narrowing". It narrows nothing: 300 files and 7436 cases still run. The underlying fixture fragility spans 13 files owned by other tasks and its two directions need OPPOSITE repairs, so it is reported (to #workers msg-fdfd52ba for task-90283f0f, and to the governor) and deliberately NOT patched from this lane.
B. INSTALLED-CLAUDE ARMS (4 cases). claude-host-runtime.test.ts, claude-runtime-request.test.ts x2 and claude-runtime-discovery.test.ts hard-require a real claude.exe under a governor ruling of 2026-08-16 02:10Z (option (a): hard-fail, never skip). A runner has none. I refused to reverse a governor ruling myself and escalated with the measurement; governor ruling 2026-08-19 (msg-0bf62be7 -> msg-44487079) amended it to option (a) SCOPED AMENDMENT, and I implemented exactly the conditions: skip only when `WIN && process.env.CI === "true" && installedClaudeExecutable() === null`, the ruling named in a comment at each site, and disclosure in the completion note. A developer box without claude.exe still HARD-FAILS, and the non-Windows branches of those same tests still run on ubuntu/macos because the predicate requires WIN.

MY OWN TWO TIMEOUT FIXES THIS STEP (both real, neither a mask): codex-stream.test.ts builds a MAX_FRAMED_LINES stream — pure CPU volume that outran the 5s default on a two-core runner (suite pinned 30s, focused 13/13); claude-runtime-discovery's "answers the same runtime whether or not a caller passes a steering argument" is the only case there that searches the REAL host PATH, twice, and it blew 5s on a loaded local box (pinned 30s, focused 10/10).

The 5 skips in the green run are the 4 governor-approved CI arms plus the pre-existing off-Windows boundary case; locally, where the CLI and the native binaries exist, the same suite skips only 2 and runs those 4 for real.

ADVERSARIAL REVIEW of my own diff (7 files, all mine, no foreign file in any of my six commits):
- Fail-closed on the Test leg: if `pnpm test` dies before writing vitest-windows.log, Select-String yields nothing, `-not` is true, and the step exits 1 with its ::error:: annotation. A missing log can never read as a pass.
- Ordering: exit status is checked BEFORE the count line, so a red run reports "pnpm test exited N" rather than being mislabelled as vacuous.
- Why the two preference pins: a pwsh step defaults to ErrorActionPreference=Stop, under which a native command's redirected stderr can abort the step. Git's "LF will be replaced by CRLF" warning appears in every one of these runs, so this was a live hazard, not a theoretical one.
- Cache poisoning: the green run logs `Cache saved with the key: node-cache-Windows-x64-pnpm-c5e074ff...` and pnpm/action-setup resolved `cache_dependency_path: pnpm-lock.yaml` — content-keyed on the lockfile, and `--frozen-lockfile` means a poisoned cache still cannot change the dependency set.
- Windows path length: checkout of 3689 files succeeded on every run; no core.longpaths override was needed, so none was added.
- Concurrent pushes: no `concurrency:` group, deliberately — one would cancel in-flight runs of the three foreign jobs too. Runs queue instead, each grades its own sha, and every claim here is pinned to a sha.
- The skipIf predicate, checked in both directions rather than reasoned about: it requires WIN, and the ubuntu leg of the green run shows the three files running with ZERO skips (43, 11, 10 tests, all green), so the non-Windows legs are untouched. It requires CI === "true", and a clean clone of the SAME commit on this developer box runs those four arms for real: 2 skipped locally vs 5 in CI, where the CI per-file lines are exactly request 2 + host-runtime 1 + discovery 1 + the pre-existing off-Windows smoke 1.
- Timeout pins raise ceilings only; no assertion, reason code or arm was weakened. Cost if something genuinely hangs: 30s to fail instead of 5s.
- The smoke's 12s trigger budget: on the runner that file took 28.65s for 5 tests, so the pre-assert work fits with room. Residual risk noted, not hidden: a runner slower than this by ~8x could re-race it.
- Small blemish, disclosed: my new `installedClaudeExecutable()` in claude-runtime-discovery.test.ts omits the realpathSync its two siblings apply. It feeds a boolean predicate only, never a path, so the difference cannot leak into an assertion.
- Residual by design: with TEMP pinned, the lane no longer exercises 8.3-mangled temp paths. That fragility is real, spans 13 files owned by other tasks, needs opposite repairs in its two directions, and is reported to #workers (msg-fdfd52ba, for task-90283f0f) and to the governor rather than patched from here.
